habitat.label: Exploration vehicle
habitat.source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge brief; NASA exploration vehicle atmosphere 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2
habitat.line: Exploration vehicle: gravity 0 m/s², pressure 10.2 psia, O₂ 26.5%, vent speed 10 cm/s (assumed), flame size 10 mm (assumed).

verdicts.label: Prevention
verdicts.rule: evidence if M3 (gas flames) and M4 (SAFFIRE solids) are both covered at this habitat; partial if exactly one is; no evidence if neither is.
verdicts.because: M3 (gas flame self-extinction) is covered at this habitat; M4 (SAFFIRE solid-material burn extent) has no evidence here.

verdicts.label: Flame behaviour
verdicts.rule: evidence if M1, M2 and M5 are all covered at this habitat; partial if one or two are; no evidence if none is.
verdicts.because: M1 (droplet flame self-extinction) and M2 (droplet extinction diameter) are covered at this habitat; M5 (SPICE coflow flame window) has no evidence here.

verdicts.label: Detection
verdicts.rule: always partial: smoke sizes were measured (SAME-R) and a simulation compares Earth gravity with microgravity (PSI-115), but there are no lunar dust data and no cited detector size sensitivity, and none of this evidence depends on the habitat's pressure or O2 (ADR-0007).
verdicts.because: Smoke particle sizes from heated spacecraft materials were measured (SAME-R, PSI-101) and one smoke-versus-dust size comparison exists (Arizona Road Dust, DAFT, PSI-47), but there are no lunar dust data and no cited source for which particle sizes detectors respond to. This evidence does not depend on the habitat's pressure or O₂. Only the PSI-115 simulation is about gravity, and its microgravity case matches this habitat.

verdicts.label: Suppression
verdicts.rule: evidence if the R2 dilution curves have covered points (fraction > 0, M1 applicable) for both CO2 and helium; partial if for one of them; no evidence if for neither.
verdicts.because: FLEX dilution tests cover this atmosphere for CO₂ up to 50% (10 of 14 diluted points) and helium up to 45% (14 of 14 diluted points); these show how dilution changed droplet flames in tests, not how an extinguisher performs.

key_numbers.label: P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout)
key_numbers.text: M1 P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout): 69.8% (90% band 38.7% to 87.9%); transfer confidence high.

key_numbers.label: Extinction diameter
key_numbers.text: M2 Extinction diameter: 3.38 mm (90% band 2.01 mm to 4.12 mm); transfer confidence high.

key_numbers.label: P(gas flame self-extinguishes vs flow-terminated)
key_numbers.text: M3 P(gas flame self-extinguishes vs flow-terminated): 94.7% (90% band 88.4% to 98.5%); transfer confidence high.

gaps.label: Solid material burn extent
gaps.reason: extrapolation, no evidence: SAFFIRE-II only tested ~22% O2 (21.5-22.1%) at ~1 atm cabin pressure and 20 cm/s flow; habitat O2 26.5% outside 20-24.0%; pressure 10.2 psia (0.69 atm) outside 0.9-1.1 atm. No estimate is given outside the tested atmosphere.

nearest_point.assumed: pressure not in the PSI table; ~1 atm assumed

gaps.text: M4 Solid material burn extent: no evidence at this habitat. Nearest tested atmosphere: 22.1% O₂ at 14.7 psia (PSI-99, 6 tests), atmosphere distance 1.5. That point is partly assumed: pressure not in the PSI table; ~1 atm assumed. Rule: Covered only inside the SAFFIRE-II tested box (O2 20-24%, 0.9-1.1 atm).

gaps.label: Supported coflow window
gaps.reason: extrapolation, no evidence: SPICE only tested in ISS cabin air (assumed ~21% O2 / ~1 atm; the table records no atmosphere); habitat O2 26.5% outside 19-23.5%; pressure 10.2 psia (0.69 atm) outside 0.9-1.1 atm. No estimate is given outside the tested atmosphere.

nearest_point.assumed: SPICE table records no atmosphere; ISS cabin air (~21% O2, ~1 atm) assumed

gaps.text: M5 Supported coflow window: no evidence at this habitat. Nearest tested atmosphere: 21% O₂ at 14.7 psia (PSI-107, 431 tests), atmosphere distance 1.64. That point is partly assumed: SPICE table records no atmosphere; ISS cabin air (~21% O2, ~1 atm) assumed. Rule: Covered only inside ISS-cabin-like air (O2 19-23.5%, 0.9-1.1 atm).

No lunar dust or lunar dust simulant data exists in these PSI files. The only dust measured (DAFT) is Arizona Road Dust. So "could lunar dust fool a smoke detector?" is an open question here, not an answered one.
We have no cited source for which particle sizes ionization and light-scattering smoke detectors respond to, so the page does not show detector size ranges.

FLEX tested CO₂ dilution only between 14% and 24% O₂ (0.69-3.05 atm). This habitat (26% O₂, 0.69 atm) is close enough to those tests (distance <= 2, ADR-0006) for CO₂ fractions up to 50%; beyond that there is no evidence and the curve has a gap. Gravity does not change these numbers; it only widens the band (ADR-0005).
gaps.safety_note: CO₂ at these concentrations is dangerous to breathe. Spacecraft use portable CO₂ or water-mist extinguishers aimed at the fire, not cabin flooding. This shows how dilution affected flames in NASA's tests; it is not an operating procedure.

gaps.text: FLEX tested helium dilution only between 13% and 24% O₂ (0.69-1.01 atm). This habitat (26% O₂, 0.69 atm) is close enough to those tests (distance <= 2, ADR-0006) for helium fractions up to 45%. Gravity does not change these numbers; it only widens the band (ADR-0005).
gaps.safety_note: Changing a cabin's gas mix changes what the crew breathes. This shows how helium dilution affected flames in NASA's FLEX tests; it is not an operating procedure or extinguisher guidance.

next_tests.rule: Relevance = the planner's own score x its re-scoring kernel between this habitat and the candidate (atmosphere distance, gravity scale 2 m/s², vent scale 10 cm/s), in place of its three fixed target weights. A dilution candidate is a test at that cabin atmosphere with CO₂ added, so the CO₂ term is left out. Top 3 of the planner's ranked list.

items.rationale: Extinction diameter at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2, vent 10 cm/s: the current 90% band is 1.00 wide (relative), 72% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the exploration vehicle 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2 target (weight 0.70).

P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout) at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2, vent 20 cm/s: the current 90% band is 0.68 wide, 100% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the exploration vehicle 10.2 psia / 26.5% O2 target (weight 0.70).

Extinction diameter at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 8.2 psia / 34% O2, vent 20 cm/s: there is no microgravity evidence at this atmosphere (honesty gate), 100% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the lunar/Mars base 8.2 psia / 34% O2 target (weight 1.00).

history.rule: Closest R1 incident atmosphere by atmosphere distance (O₂ and pressure); shown only within distance 2, the same reach as the honesty gate.
history.text: Artemis II smoke alarm (2026) and Mir oxygen-generator fire (1997) happened at 21% O₂ and 14.7 psia, atmosphere distance 1.64 from this habitat (the incident's atmosphere is an assumed value, not a recorded one). Gravity there was 0 m/s² as here. The replay shows what today's data say about those conditions; it does not judge what happened.

trust.text: Honesty test (ADR-0009): hiding one tested atmosphere at a time and refitting, the 90% band held for 72 of 74 M1 atmospheres, 58 of 65 M2 atmospheres and 78 of 83 M3 atmospheres under the overlap rule, which is lenient for groups of 1-3 tests. Under the strict rule (observed share inside the band) it held for 7 of 74 (M1) and 4 of 83 (M3). In the wide check (a whole 0.10 O₂ band hidden at once) M3 had only 9 covered groups, a weak test. The test ran in microgravity (0 g), so the gravity widening of partial-gravity bands is not tested by it.
